subject: Zenith trial onramp: success criteria & capacity ask
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@zenith.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@zenith.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Zenith trial onramp: success criteria & capacity ask

Hi Asha / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into the trial planning phase.

Recap of discovery:
- Goal: 3-week evaluation of Redwood inference for real-time customer-facing chat & question-answer flows.
- Target workload: 40 sustained QPS during business hours with peaks up to ~120 QPS for short bursts (sales events).
- Quality baseline: internal pass-rate of our golden prompts >= 85% (we’ll run the eval harness you and we agreed on).

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: P95 generation <= 200ms for 512-token request profile (90% of requests).
2) Throughput: support 40 sustained QPS with <2% error rate for the core 3-week window.
3) Quality: evaluation score >= 0.85 against your acceptance prompt set.
4) Ops: model stable with no more than two incident escalations and documented runbook.

Capacity & onramp ask (what we’d like from you):
- Baseline reserved capacity: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (we’ll run on your cloud account).
- Burst allowance: up to 8 GPUs for short windows (we’ll coordinate scheduling and cost exposure).
- Autoscaling policy: CPU/GPU utilization-based scale up/down with a hard cap at burst GPUs. Suggest scale-up threshold 75% GPU util sustained for 60s, scale-down at 40% for 3m.

Who does what:
- You (Zenith): share sample dataset (anonymized), cloud account role for provisioning, and PO/trial approval.
- Redwood: allocate baseline GPUs, run eval harness, provide daily latency/usage dashboard, and a weekly checkpoint.
- Project owners: Asha (Zenith) / Jordan (Redwood) primary leads. Dev (Redwood) engineering lead for infra. Marissa (Redwood) will own procurement/credits.

Attachments: trial scope draft, cost estimate, sample schema.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Asha to confirm success criteria and provide sample dataset by EOD 2028-03-22.
2) Zenith to provide cloud account and PO outline week of 2028-03-27.
3) Redwood to provision baseline GPUs and run a dry run week of 2028-04-03, full trial week of 2028-04-10.

If that all looks good I’ll send a shorter mutual action plan doc and a DocuSign for the trial PO.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@zenith.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@zenith.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith trial onramp: success criteria & capacity ask

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary, much appreciated. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Success criteria look good; we’ll validate the 0.85 quality threshold internally and flag any edge cases.
- I’ll upload an anonymized sample dataset (chat logs and expected outputs) by EOD today to the Google Drive link — Tom is looping in infra details.
- On data retention and privacy: we need clarification on token-level logging retention. We won’t send PII; still, can Redwood confirm logs are retained for a max of 30 days for this trial unless we request otherwise?

Regarding timing: we prefer the trial start the week of 2028-04-10 (to align with our product sprint). If possible, can the dry run shift a week earlier (week of 2028-03-27) so we can validate end-to-end before the sprint block?

I’ll also ask procurement for a short PO template and loop Tom for cloud account details.

—Asha
Asha Kapoor
Head of Product, Zenith AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@zenith.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@zenith.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith trial onramp: success criteria & capacity ask

Looping in procurement details / quick checklist so we don’t get blocked:

Procurement checklist for trial: 
- Trial PO min: brief one-page PO is sufficient (term: 3-week evaluation, non-binding, cost cover or credit arrangement).
- Required fields from Zenith: billing contact, billing address, PO number, expected start date.
- Compliance: sign Acknowledgement of our trial DPA addendum (I’ll attach a short DPA).

We should also capture credit limits for burst GPUs — recommend we offer an initial credit cap of $7,500 for burst usage and request pre-approval to expand. If Zenith prefers to manage billing directly on their cloud account, we’ll coordinate provisioning access only.

I’ve attached a one-pager PO template and the DPA stub for quick review. Once Asha confirms dataset + retention policy we can issue the DocuSign for the PO.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@zenith.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@zenith.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith trial onramp: success criteria & capacity ask

Thanks Jordan / Asha. Quick infra notes from my side: we can grant a service account with IAM role for provisioning. I’ll send the specific role and temporary key to Dev once procurement confirms the PO path.

A couple clarifications on capacity:
- We are comfortable with baseline 4x A100-equivalent GPUs.
- On burst, our cloud budget team prefers a cap at 6 GPUs not 8 — can Redwood accommodate a 6-GPU hard cap for burst windows?
- We’d like autoscaling safety: please enforce a cost-protect guardrail that pauses burst scaling if hourly spend > $1,200 for a single hour and notify us.

Also, regarding logs: we can accept 30-day retention for the trial. Please confirm you’ll redact any token-level PII if it appears.

I’ll upload credentials to a secure vault and ping Dev.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Cloud Engineering, Zenith AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@zenith.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@zenith.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith trial onramp: success criteria & capacity ask

Perfect — thanks everyone, below is an updated, agreed-on plan for records and next steps. I’ll convert to a mutual action plan after you confirm the few inline items.

Agreed on high level:
- Trial length: 3 weeks (evaluation window) with a dry run week earlier as requested. Dry run: week of 2028-03-27. Full trial: week of 2028-04-10.
- Success criteria: Latency P95 <= 200ms, sustained throughput 40 QPS, quality >= 0.85.
- Capacity: Baseline 4x A100-equivalent GPUs; burst cap agreed to 6 GPUs (Tom’s request).
- Autoscaling: scale up at 75% GPU util for 60s, scale down at 40% for 3m. Hard caps applied per Zen account. Redwood to enforce hourly cost guardrail of $1,200 (pause burst and alert).
- Data retention: logs retained 30 days for the trial; Redwood to redact token-level PII.
- Credits & billing: Redwood offers $7,500 initial burst credit; if Zenith wants to manage cloud billing directly, they will provide service account and we will provision into their account.

Owners & checkpoints:
- Pre-trial dry run (Jordan / Dev): validate provisioning and run the smoke test (by 2028-03-30).
- Week 1 checkpoint (Asha, Jordan, Marissa): baseline performance & quality check.
- Weekly cadence during trial for dashboards and notes; final readout 1 week after trial end.

Action items (who/when):
- Asha: share sample dataset and cloud billing contact by EOD 2028-03-22.
- Tom: upload service account role/credentials to secure vault for Dev by 2028-03-24.
- Marissa: send DocuSign PO + DPA stub to Asha for signature (target 2028-03-24).
- Dev: prepare provisioning scripts and dry-run checklist by 2028-03-26.

I’ll draft the mutual action plan and the DocuSign PO once Marissa confirms the template fields. Thanks all — excited to get this underway.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
